Work includes evaluating structural, building envelope, mechanical, electrical, and site infrastructure components in accordance with recognized codes, standards, and industry practices.

 Coordinate site inspections and assessment activities with property representatives, facility personnel, and internal project teams.

 Experience managing assessment projects, including site investigations, reporting, schedules, budgets, and client deliverables.
 Working knowledge of structural, building envelope, mechanical, electrical, and site infrastructure systems.
 Experience preparing technical reports, lifecycle assessments, capital plans, repair recommendations, and Class D cost estimates.
 Knowledge of applicable standards and regulatory requirements, including ASTM E2018 and provincial building codes.

Our culture 
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first.

Position Summary 
 As Product Owner for Sadie, you will be responsible for turning our product vision and roadmap into clearly defined, deliverable product outcomes.
 You will work closely with management, customers, engineering, design, and commercial teams to understand what needs to be built, define how it should work, and ensure it is delivered successfully.
 A major part of your role will be translating product ideas and customer problems into clear requirements, workflows, tickets, acceptance criteria, and expected behaviours that engineering can execute against.
 You will own the detail behind the roadmap and ensure what we ship fulfils the original product and customer intent.
 Values 
 Excellent communication and collaboration skills
 Strong ownership and accountability
 Customer-focused and outcome-driven
 Highly organized with strong attention to detail
 Comfortable challenging assumptions and asking questions
 Open to feedback and continuous improvement
 High degree of integrity, professionalism, and discretion
 What You’ll Be Doing 
 Work closely with management to translate the Sadie product vision and roadmap into actionable product initiatives.
 Own and maintain the product backlog, ensuring priorities are clearly defined and aligned with the roadmap.
 Break larger product initiatives into clear requirements, user stories, workflows, tickets, and acceptance criteria.
 Define exactly how Sadie should behave across different customer scenarios and edge cases.
 Ensure engineering has the context and requirements needed to build features correctly without ambiguity.
 Work closely with engineering throughout development to answer questions, resolve ambiguity, make trade-offs, and keep delivery aligned with the intended product outcome.
 Review and validate completed work against requirements and acceptance criteria before release.
 Test Sadie across real-world scenarios to ensure features and behaviours work as intended.
 Review real customer calls, feedback, and product usage to identify gaps, edge cases, and opportunities for improvement.
 Work with customers and internal teams to understand problems and translate feedback into actionable product requirements.
 Coordinate product pilots and releases, including defining scope, expected behaviour, success criteria, and feedback loops.
 Identify dependencies, blockers, risks, and missing requirements before they impact delivery.
 Maintain clear documentation around product functionality, decisions, requirements, and expected behaviour.
 Track progress against the roadmap and communicate product status, blockers, and changes to relevant stakeholders.
 Ensure features are not simply shipped, but actually fulfil the original product vision and solve the intended customer problem.
 Continuously improve how requirements are defined, communicated, tested, and delivered across the product organization.
 What You Bring 
 2+ years of experience as a Product Owner, Business Analyst, or similar product-focused role.
 Experience working closely with software engineering teams to deliver customer-facing products.
 Strong ability to take a high-level product idea and turn it into detailed, actionable requirements.
 Experience writing clear product tickets, user stories, acceptance criteria, and functional requirements.
 Strong understanding of product workflows, user journeys, edge cases, and expected system behaviours.
 Experience managing and prioritizing a product backlog.
 Strong attention to detail and the ability to identify gaps or ambiguity before development begins.
 Ability to understand technical concepts sufficiently to communicate effectively with engineering teams.
 Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to make pragmatic decisions when requirements or priorities change.
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
 Ability to manage multiple initiatives and priorities in a fast-moving environment.
 Strong sense of ownership and accountability for the quality of the final product, not just the completion of tickets.
 Pluses 
 Experience working on conversational, voice, communications, or workflow products.
 Experience working with hospitality, restaurants, hotels, or other service-based businesses.
 Experience managing complex products with multiple integrations and dependencies.
 Experience working in a startup or fast-moving product environment.
 Comfortable working in an environment where the roadmap evolves quickly based on customer and business needs.
 Am I Right for This Position? 
 You will be a strong fit if you enjoy taking an idea that may initially be high-level or ambiguous and turning it into something an engineering team can confidently build.
 You should naturally think about questions like:
 What exactly should happen? What happens if something goes wrong? What are the edge cases? What does success look like? Does what we built actually match what we intended?
 You do not need to be an engineer. You do need to be comfortable working closely with engineers and taking ownership of the detail required to turn a product vision into a working product.
 Why Is This Job Important? 
 Sadie is evolving quickly, and our ability to execute on our product vision depends on turning ideas and customer needs into clear, well-defined work for our engineering teams.
 The Product Owner sits between vision and execution.
 Your responsibility is to make sure the roadmap does not remain a collection of ideas. It becomes clearly defined functionality that engineering can build, customers can use, and the business can measure.
 What Will I Learn in This Position? 
 You will gain hands-on experience building and scaling a rapidly evolving technology product used in real customer interactions every day.
 You will work closely with leadership, engineering, customers, and commercial teams and develop a deep understanding of how product strategy is translated into requirements, delivered through engineering, validated with customers, and continuously improved.

The Staff Product Manager is an Individual Contributor (IC) product leader responsible for a broad platform surface for Atlas Infinite at MongoDB. Atlas Infinite is the largest architectural innovation in MongoDB Atlas ever, purpose-built to handle today's speed and scale of development and demand. 
 In this position, you will own and solve end-to-end problems around the user experience and database experience of Atlas Infinite, including but limited to feature discovery, activation, monetization, and retention. You will see patterns, opportunities, and risks across areas, own cross-team product and architectural trade-offs, establish reusable standards for PM craft, and align senior stakeholders around multi-year bets. You have deep knowledge of cloud database platforms, distributed data systems, and enterprise product development.
 You will partner closely with cross-functional engineering leaders, product peers, and executive stakeholders to drive outcomes across organizational boundaries, guiding a portfolio spanning Atlas Infinite's disaggregated compute and storage architecture, production workload readiness, migration and Atlas interoperability, and the new customer experiences this architecture may make possible. You will not inherit a closed list of future features: part of your mandate is to discover opportunities we have not yet articulated and challenge assumptions about which problems matter most. With AWS public preview now live, you will help turn real workload evidence into a credible path to GA and subsequent releases, in close partnership with the existing team.
 This role can be based out of a MongoDB office or remotely in Canada.
 Responsibilities
 Interlinked Vision & Multi-Year Bets: Set and champion a product vision across Atlas Infinite's capabilities, while actively discovering opportunities that are not on today's roadmap or fit any single team's remit. Explore what decoupled compute and storage could make possible for developers, enterprises, and emerging AI workloads; use hypotheses, customer evidence, prototypes, and market signals to uncover needs we have not yet named. Branching, on-demand compute, and instant recovery are examples of possible bets. Make the case for investment and prioritization, including build-vs-buy considerations, and distinguish exploratory vision from release commitments
 Cross-Team Execution: Along with program management, own execution health across workstreams, negotiating sequencing, scope, and resource trade-offs with engineering leaders and peer PMs where you have no direct authority. Ensure preview-to-GA readiness, roadmaps, and dependencies across database, storage, Atlas platform, migration, backup, security, and cloud infrastructure teams are aligned and connect to company objectives
 Execution & Research Standards: Establish lightweight operating practices and shared customer/market research frameworks that make workload qualification, customer-representative testing, win/loss analysis, launch readiness, and post-launch learning consistent across the portfolio. Use data to drive decisions without overburdening delivery teams
 Product Health: Resolve complex post-launch escalations when the root cause spans architecture, performance, migration, observability, supportability, or unclear ownership. Turn customer and operational signals into systemic product fixes rather than one-off workarounds
 Customer Discovery: Identify needs and competitive dynamics that cut across product areas. Look beyond requests from today's customers to discover emerging jobs-to-be-done, surprising uses of the architecture, and reasons customers do not choose MongoDB at all. Combine interviews, workload and pricing evidence, product analytics, field feedback, and experiments to test known hypotheses and uncover unknowns; reorient the roadmap when the evidence warrants it
 Outbound & GTM: Partner with product marketing, pricing, sales, solutions architecture, customer success, documentation, and support on high-stakes customer engagements, product positioning, and omni-channel marketing. Establish ideal customer profile; ensure claims and migration guidance match demonstrated capabilities; translate successful adoption and enablement approaches into shared playbooks
 Executive Alignment: Synthesize customer experience, technical readiness, adoption, and commercial impact into clear, confident product stories for senior leadership. Surface cross-area risks and progress early, including trade-offs between new-workload growth, customer savings, and changes to existing Atlas usage
 Mentorship: Mentor PMs across the area, sharing frameworks for cross-team alignment, customer evidence, technical trade-offs, multi-year bets, and leadership communication
 Qualifications
 8+ years of product management or equivalent product leadership experience, with a track record personally shaping strategy and outcomes for complex technical platforms across multiple teams, rather than only coordinating delivery
 Strong technical fluency in cloud databases, distributed data systems, storage infrastructure, developer experiences, or an adjacent developer platform. Able to reason with engineers about architecture, performance, availability, data movement, and trade-offs without needing to be the system designer
 A demonstrated ability to discover opportunities beyond the current roadmap: connect technical possibilities to unmet customer needs, formulate and test hypotheses, notice surprising patterns, and change direction when evidence challenges the original thesis
 Experience taking a complex product from early adoption toward dependable, broader use while protecting space for longer-term innovation; able to make explicit trade-offs among customer trust, technical readiness, speed, and investment
 Proven ability to influence without authority, negotiating sequencing and resource trade-offs across partner teams with competing priorities
 Commercial and analytical judgment: able to assess workload-level value, adoption and usage evidence, competitive alternatives, pricing and unit economics, and the impact of a new product on an existing portfolio. Comfortable with build-vs-buy questions where relevant
 Ability to raise the quality of customer discovery and product decision-making across teams through useful shared methods and mentorship, without mistaking more process for better outcomes
 Exceptional communication skills: able to explain a technical and commercial thesis, its uncertainties, and the evidence that would change your mind to engineers, customers, executives, and go-to-market partners
 Success Measures
 In 3 months you will have built a shared picture of which workloads Atlas Infinite serves well today, where customers struggle, what must be true for broader adoption, and what remains unknown. You will have clarified ownership with peer PMs and engineering, established baseline measures, and identified the highest-value questions to investigate

At Poka, we're changing how the world's industrial teams work — capturing the knowledge of their best people and putting it in every operator's hands. 
 Our connected worker platform is purpose-built for manufacturing and the wider industrial world, with industrial AI inside the shift, not on top of it. The result: frontline performance that becomes compounding knowledge and measurable impact — every shift, every site, every region. 
 We're proud to support global leaders like Nestlé, Bosch, Mars, and Danone across 3,000+ sites in 70+ countries. And as a fast-growing part of the IFS family, you'll join a team whose daily work directly shapes the platform behind how modern manufacturing gets done. 
 Role overview 
 Our team develops the AI assistant built into Poka. Workers and supervisors use it every day on manufacturing floors. We build it with prompts, tools, information retrieval and agents.
 As a quality assurance (QA) specialist on this team, you make sure what we ship works: the assistant's answers and the features around it. You do it with automation, AI and tools you build, not with manual testing. You work with the devs, the product team and the design team to define what "good" means, then you build the evals, automated tests and tools that check it.
 How this is different from traditional QA 
 No manual test passes. If something needs to be checked more than once, you automate it, with code, AI or whatever tool fits.
 A large part of what you test has no single answer. The same question can get 50 good answers phrased differently, and the assistant can answer differently from one run to the next. You help define what "good" means and measure it.
 You write Python every week.
 If you're looking for a role focused on test plans and manual regression testing, this isn't it.
 What you'll be responsible for 
 Automating QA for the team's features and building the tools that make it easier, including ways for non-developers to add evals and analyze the results.
 Building and maintaining eval suites based on real usage: actual user questions, expected behavior and the edge cases that show up in production.
 Defining with the team what a good answer looks like for our users, writing scoring rubrics and using LLM-as-judge where it makes sense, calibrated against human-labeled samples.
 Running regression checks in CI every time we change a prompt, a tool, retrieval or the Claude model version, covering answer quality, cost and speed. You build the guardrails, evals and tests that tell us whether a release gets the green light or not.
 Reviewing real conversations and grouping failures into patterns: made-up answers, wrong tool calls, missed context, inappropriate tone. Then working with developers to turn them into fixes.
 Contributing to adversarial testing: prompt injection, data leaking between customers, getting the assistant to do things it shouldn't.
 Doing timeboxed exploratory testing on features that change what the assistant can decide or do, like new agents, tools or actions, including checking that actions stay safe when something fails or gets retried.
 Joining feature kickoffs to help define acceptance criteria, including AI-specific ones.
 What you bring 
 AEC, DEC or BAC in a field related to the position, or equivalent experience
 2 to 4 years of relevant experience
 A background in test automation or as an SDET
 You're comfortable with several programming languages, including Python and TypeScript
 Real curiosity about how LLMs behave and why they fail
 You're comfortable judging quality when there's no single answer, and explaining your reasoning

 Position Summary (Purpose of Job) 
 The Lead Infrastructure Architect defines and governs enterprise infrastructure architecture across hybrid and public cloud, compute, virtualization, storage, data protection, data center and colocation services, identity foundations, resilience, supporting platform services, and the connectivity dependencies required to support compute and platform workloads. The role establishes target-state architectures, reference patterns, standards, and multiyear roadmaps that improve reliability, security, scalability, cost efficiency, operational performance, and business agility. 
 Operating with the highest level of autonomy, the Lead Infrastructure Architect partners with enterprise architecture, cybersecurity, engineering, operations, application teams, service owners, and business stakeholders to evaluate technology options, guide workload-placement decisions, validate infrastructure designs, and lead migration planning from current-state platforms to strategic target architectures. The role provides final infrastructure architecture recommendations and governs exceptions through established architecture decision forums. 
 The role provides technical leadership for enterprise transformation initiatives, including hybrid-cloud adoption, platform modernization, legacy retirement, data center and colocation evolution, resilience improvement, technical debt reduction, and M&A integration or separation. The architect translates complex technical options into clear business decisions by articulating value, cost, risk, dependencies, operational impact, and implementation tradeoffs for technical and nontechnical leaders. 
 Key Responsibilities 
 •  Set infrastructure strategy and roadmaps. Define target-state architectures and multiyear roadmaps across cloud, compute, virtualization, storage, backup and recovery, connectivity dependencies for compute and platform workloads, colocation, and shared infrastructure platform services. Align roadmaps across infrastructure, security, application, and enterprise architecture domains. 
 •  Establish workload-placement direction. Define decision principles for placing workloads across public cloud, private cloud, on-premises, colocation, and distributed infrastructure based on business criticality, security, performance, resilience, regulatory requirements, cost, latency, and operational supportability. 
 •  Design end-to-end infrastructure solutions. Translate business and technical requirements into logical and physical infrastructure architectures. Validate capacity, performance, availability, recovery, security, observability, automation, and supportability for high-impact initiatives. 
 •  Lead infrastructure modernization. Provide architecture leadership for hybrid-cloud adoption, virtualization modernization, platform consolidation, data center and colocation transitions, technology currency, and legacy-platform retirement. Define transition states, migration waves, dependencies, and risk controls. 
 •  Govern standards and exceptions. Own infrastructure reference architectures, approved patterns, technology standards, architecture decision records, and design-assurance criteria. Lead enterprise quality reviews and manage exceptions through the appropriate governance forums. 
 •  Drive resilience and recovery architecture. Define patterns for high availability, backup, disaster recovery, cyber recovery, geographic redundancy, and service continuity. Ensure designs align to service-level objectives, recovery-time and recovery-point objectives, failure-domain requirements, and recovery-testing expectations. 
 •  Direct implementation and operational transition. Guide engineering teams through implementation and modification activities, resolve complex cross-platform design issues, and ensure solutions are deployable, observable, supportable, testable, and sustainable in steady-state operations. 
 •  Institutionalize well-architected practices. Embed security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, sustainability, and operational excellence into infrastructure designs. Establish architecture KPIs and OKRs and recommend adjustments that accelerate measurable value. 
 •  Optimize cost and lifecycle value. Develop architecture options that address total cost of ownership, capacity, consumption, licensing, vendor support, platform lifecycle, and avoided-cost opportunities. Ensure modernization creates a clear path to retire displaced platforms and reduce duplication. 
 •  Evaluate strategic technologies and vendors. Assess architectural fit, interoperability, product roadmap, support model, lifecycle risk, concentration risk, commercial implications, and alignment to enterprise standards. Provide fact-based recommendations and reference implementations. 
 •  Influence and coach. Communicate architecture options, risks, and tradeoffs to senior leaders and nontechnical stakeholders. Mentor architects and engineers, strengthen architecture practices, and drive adoption of modern platform engineering, DevOps, automation, and infrastructure-as-code approaches.  
 •  Oversee M&A infrastructure architecture. Lead infrastructure due diligence, separation and integration planning, transitional-state design, dependency analysis, migration sequencing, and risk mitigation. Align technical teams and senior stakeholders to the target-state infrastructure vision.  
 Minimum Requirements  
 •  Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience and typically 10+ years of relevant infrastructure architecture or engineering experience. Fewer years may be accepted with relevant Master’s or Doctorate qualifications.  
 •  Sustained leadership of enterprise-scale, cross-platform infrastructure programs in complex or regulated environments.  
 Critical Skills (Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities)  
 •  Enterprise infrastructure architecture mastery. Deep experience across hybrid cloud, compute, virtualization, storage, data protection, colocation, shared platform services, and the infrastructure connectivity dependencies required to support those environments.  
 •  Architecture strategy and governance. Demonstrated ownership of target-state roadmaps, reference architectures, standards, decision frameworks, architecture decision records, design assurance, and exception management. Working knowledge of TOGAF concepts and ADM is preferred.  
 •  Hybrid and multicloud architecture. Experience with workload placement, landing-zone dependencies, compute and platform connectivity requirements, identity, security, observability, automation, governance, and cost management across one or more major cloud platforms.  
 •  Infrastructure modernization and migration. Proven ability to lead legacy retirement, platform consolidation, technical debt reduction, data center or colocation transitions, technology currency, and complex migration planning.  
 •  Resilience architecture. Expertise in high availability, backup, disaster recovery, cyber recovery, failure-domain design, geographic resilience, RTO/RPO alignment, and recovery validation.  
 •  Infrastructure automation and platform engineering. Strong understanding of infrastructure as code, configuration management, policy as code, CI/CD, observability, self-service platform patterns, and automated compliance controls.  
 •  Security by design. Ability to apply zero-trust principles, identity and privileged-access controls, segmentation, encryption, vulnerability management, secure configuration, and regulatory requirements to infrastructure patterns.  
 •  IT service management alignment. Knowledge of ITIL 4 service value system and practices, with the ability to ensure supportability, service ownership, operational readiness, and lifecycle governance.  
 •  Architecture visualization and documentation. Proficiency with C4, ArchiMate, or equivalent methods to communicate context, dependencies, components, interfaces, decisions, and tradeoffs to executive, product, engineering, security, and operations audiences.  
 •  Financial and commercial acumen. Ability to develop TCO comparisons, value cases, capacity and consumption models, licensing considerations, and vendor-platform tradeoffs.  
 •  Executive storytelling and decision rigor. Ability to frame options, value, cost, risk, dependencies, and tradeoffs with clear, implementable guidance for nontechnical audiences. 
 •  Technical leadership. Ability to influence without direct authority, coach architects and engineers, resolve cross-domain decisions, and build alignment across enterprise architecture, security, engineering, operations, and business stakeholders.  
 •  L5 competency proficiency. Adaptability; Architecture and Master Planning; Collaboration and Partnership; Communication and Internal Marketing; Design Thinking; Digital Acumen; Problem Solving; Strategic Decision Making; Business Function Knowledge; Customer and Business Driven; and Leadership, all at Leading proficiency.  
 Additional Qualifications  
 •  Advanced architecture expertise in one or more major cloud or infrastructure platforms, supported by relevant certifications or equivalent demonstrated enterprise experience.  
 •  Proven record of defining infrastructure standards and owning governance, exception management, and portfolio or enterprise architecture quality reviews.  
 •  Demonstrated leadership from capability strategy and roadmap through implementation, migration, operational transition, and steady-state optimization.  
 •  Experience aligning product, application, cybersecurity, engineering, operations, and service-management teams to operationalize target architectures and achieve measurable outcomes.  
 •  Experience developing or contributing to business cases, TCO analysis, vendor evaluations, capacity planning, licensing optimization, and investment decisions.  
 •  Experience establishing measurable architecture outcomes such as reliability improvement, resilience, risk reduction, platform adoption, technical debt retirement, cost efficiency, and operational performance.  
 •  Experience supporting M&A infrastructure due diligence, integration, separation, or transition-service planning is preferred.

 Great design isn’t just decoration. It’s salesmanship in pixels. 
 If you’re excited by the idea of setting the creative standard across a fast-growing health and wellness brand, you might just be the Creative Director we’re looking for.
 This job will give you ALL the feels:
 At AlgaeCal, we’re driven by a single idea. To end the fear of bone loss. In the United States, an estimated 54 million people have low bone density. 
 The good news? AlgaeCal has the world’s only clinically-backed natural solution to this problem. We give hope to everyone worried about bone loss. If that excites you, you’ll find no better place to continue your career than at AlgaeCal.
 Here’s what you’ll be up to in this busy role: 
 Setting the visual standard for AlgaeCal. You’ll define what great looks like, make sure the team understands it, and keep every campaign, launch, website, ad, and brand asset moving in the same direction.
 Leading and developing a team of designers and creative specialists. You’ll review work, give clear direction, challenge weak ideas, and help strong creatives become even better.
 Protecting the brand without letting it go stale. You’ll make sure the work feels unmistakably AlgaeCal while still pushing the team to find fresher, smarter ways to bring ideas to life.
 Making the creative process better. If briefs are unclear, feedback is messy, or projects are getting stuck in revision hell, you’ll fix the system instead of just working around it.
 Using performance data to improve the work. You’ll look at what gets attention, what converts, and what falls flat, then use those lessons to guide the team’s next round of advert creatives.
 Building the team for where the business is going next. That means identifying skill gaps, planning future hires, developing career paths, and making sure the right people are working on the right things.
 Helping the team use AI intelligently. You’ll show designers where AI can speed up ideation, production, and workflows, without letting it replace taste, originality, or creative judgment.
 Keeping the team creatively sharp. You’ll stay on top of new design trends, tools, formats, and technology, then bring back the ideas that can genuinely make the work better.
 This job might be for you if you’ve got… 
 10+ years in design or creative, with 7+ years leading creative teams. You’ve been around long enough to know the difference between a good idea, a pretty idea, and an idea that actually moves a business.
 A proven track record leading multidisciplinary creative teams. Designers, editors, media producers, copywriters... you know how to get different creative brains working toward one clear vision.
 The ability to set creative direction, not just critique creative. You can take a business goal, customer insight, or product launch and turn it into a clear creative strategy the whole team can execute against.
 Strong commercial instincts. You understand audiences, positioning, funnels, paid media, conversion, and e-commerce. You care about great work, but you also care whether that work actually performed.
 Experience leading big, complicated creative initiatives. Product launches, integrated campaigns, brand evolutions, new markets... you’ve been the person keeping the idea strong while dozens of moving parts threaten to pull it apart.
 The confidence to influence senior stakeholders. You can walk into a room with leadership, present a bold idea, explain the thinking behind it, answer tough questions, and get people aligned.
 Experience building great creative teams. You know how to hire well, spot skill gaps, develop people, plan resources, and build a team that gets stronger as the business grows.
 A knack for fixing broken creative processes. Slow approvals, muddy briefs, revision hell, unclear ownership... you don’t just complain about these things. You fix them.
 A smart approach to AI and emerging technology. You know how to use new tools to help creative teams think faster, explore further, and produce more efficiently without sacrificing taste or originality.
 Now, time to be honest: is this really you? If you’re nodding your head and feeling that flutter of excitement, then we can’t wait to meet you.

 You’re humble, you put the team and others’ needs ahead of your own
 You’re hungry to learn more
 You’re people smart, in the sense that you’re a great teammate

Ce poste consiste à définir des méthodologies de test et des approches de métrologie, à valider la performance des composants, à analyser les résultats et à fournir une rétroaction technique aux équipes de conception et de produits. Le poste implique une collaboration avec les équipes de produits photoniques, de conception de puces et de validation, ainsi qu’avec différents groupes internes de R-D, dans un environnement d’ingénierie optique à la fine pointe de la technologie.
 Comment vous aurez un impact : 
 Développer une compréhension des composants photoniques intégrés de Ciena et mettre ces connaissances à profit pour élaborer des méthodologies de test innovantes.
 Collaborer avec les équipes de produits photoniques, de conception de puces et de validation afin de développer et de mettre en œuvre des solutions de test pour les composants optiques et les produits connexes.
 Définir, exécuter et améliorer les plans de test optiques et électro-optiques, notamment les montages de mesure, l’étalonnage, la collecte de données et l’interprétation des résultats.
 Analyser les données de test, résumer les tendances en matière de performance et fournir une rétroaction technique aux équipes de conception et de produits.
 Suivre, documenter et communiquer les progrès, les risques et les problèmes potentiels pouvant avoir une incidence sur la fonctionnalité ou la qualité des produits, ou sur les échéanciers des projets.
 Participer aux revues de conception des tests, contribuer à la documentation et effectuer les activités de suivi de projet.
 Les qualifications requises : 
 Formation : Baccalauréat en physique, en génie physique, en génie électrique, en génie optique ou dans une discipline connexe.

 Sens de l’organisation, souci du détail, curiosité technique, esprit d’initiative et désir de résoudre des problèmes et d’innover.
 Capacité à communiquer de façon claire, proactive et constructive, tant à l’oral qu’à l’écrit.
 Excellentes habilités à communiquer en français et en anglais (écrit et parlé) 
 Les atouts : 
 Expérience : Expérience pertinente avec des composants optiques acquise dans le cadre de stages, de programmes coopératifs, de laboratoires universitaires, de projets de recherche ou d’une expérience professionnelle antérieure dans l’industrie.

 Ciena’s High-Speed Photonic Component validation team contributes to the development and qualification of advanced optical components used in high-performance networking products.  Develop an understanding of Ciena’s integrated photonic components and apply that knowledge to innovative test methodologies.

 Analyze test data, summarize performance trends, and provide technical feedback to design and product teams. 
 Monitor, document, and communicate progress, risks, and potential issues that could affect product functionality, quality, or project timelines. 
 Participate in test design reviews, contribute to documentation, and conduct project follow-up activities.

 Education: Bachelor’s degree in physics, engineering physics, electrical engineering, optical engineering, or a related discipline.

 Ability to communicate clearly, proactively, and constructively in written and spoken communication.

 Education: Graduate studies in a relevant field.

KittySpout / DoggySpout   is looking for a Performance Creative Strategist to join our team! As our creative strategist, you will be responsible for the ideation, scripting, planning, and managing of the entire creative process with a heavy focus on Meta VSLs, UGC ads, and high-converting direct response ads - short and long form - that scale across our paid channels. We spend $2,000,000+ per month on Meta. We are looking to hire someone with 3+ years of experience. The ideal candidate has deep DTC experience in performance creative, runs a current AI stack in production, has experience briefing short and long form VSLs and delivers volume and quality in the same week, without being chased.
Who are we? 
 KittySpout is a premium DTC brand selling stainless steel cat water fountains, filters, and accessories. We sell across Shopify, Amazon, and Chewy, and we're one of the fastest-growing brands in the pet space — $22M+ in revenue and targeting $45-50M in 2026. We recently launched DoggySpout, expanding into an entirely new vertical and customer base. We're lean, we move fast, and every person on this team has a massive impact on the business.
What is our culture like & who is a good fit? 
 Culture-fit is our #1 factor when hiring! We have a genuine will-to-win. No work is beneath us if it moves us towards our goals. We utilize creativity to do more with less - and quickly. We use data to make decisions and live by the following three core values: work smart, overdeliver, speed is king, and better everyday. We love learning - every problem is an opportunity to grow.
 If you want a stress-free corporate 9-5 job, this isn't it. 
 If you want to challenge yourself and shape a fast-growing company, work directly with the founders, and see huge career growth by playing a big role in scaling it to $100m+... If you want to drive results with a group of passionate, smart, hardworking people, work in an environment without politics or corporate chicanery, and play a big part in our growth being hands-on and active, all while having a generous performance bonus structure — then you've come to the right place.
Key Objectives: 
 Manage the full creative process (from scripting all the way to final creative) in order to produce high converting creatives on an ongoing basis.
 Drive measurable improvements in core advertising metrics across digital channels with improved creatives.
 Script Direct response creatives
 Use data from creative performance on Meta to dissect, analyze and improve upon our creatives to continuously improve performance across our creatives.
 Work with our marketing team to come up with new creative concepts and ideas.
 Conduct strategic customer and competitor research to better optimize creative efforts
 Provide creative reports on a monthly and quarterly basis
 Decide on the next steps needed to scale Meta Ads further through better creative
 Produce a minimum of 15 ad briefs per week , maintaining volume and quality simultaneously — without being chased.
 Fully remote
 Fluent in English
 Direct Response Expertise: 3+ Years Experience with performance creative for DTC brands or working at a creative agency is a must.
 Strong analytical skills with hands-on experience interpreting performance data from platforms such as Northbeam, Facebook Ads, leveraging spreadsheets and reporting tools to extract insights, inform strategy and communicate campaign ideas and results.
 No issue working overtime or on the weekends if needed. You wouldn't know what to do with your free time if you were working less. You are passionate about your work.
 Excellent cultural fit as per our values above.
 Are excited to play a big role in scaling the company and work closely with the founders.
 Proven VSL copywriting experience on DR / performance brands
 Deep DTC Experience: You can name the brands and the spend levels behind your work — not just categories.
 Meta VSLs: Proven experience with both short and long form Meta VSLs. Long form is the bulk of what we run.
 AI Stack: You run a current AI stack in production — not one you tried once.
 Output: You deliver volume and quality in the same week, without being chased.
 Deep fluency with DTC and modern consumer brands
Examples of What You'll Be Doing: 
 Develop VSL briefings end-to-end: angle, hook, script, structure
 Design AI-driven concepts and hooks for paid video
 Partner with editors and performance marketers on testing
 Iterate strategy based on creative performance data
How Our Hiring Works & How We Operate: 
 We review applications on a rolling basis and keep strong candidates in our talent bench. If you're a great fit and the timing isn't right immediately, you'll be first in line when a spot opens. Our process has three stages:
(1) Application Review + Screening - we assess your background and experience to confirm mutual fit. 
(2) Technical Interview + Creative Brief - a short practical exercise so we can see how you think and work. 
(3) Culture Fit Interview - a final conversation with the founder to make sure this is the right team for you and you're the right person for us. 
KPIs and performance targets will be defined together before your start date so expectations are crystal clear from day one.
 Salary Expectation 
 USD $3,000 - $6,000 per month base (based on experience and expertise) + percentage of ad spend bonus structure.
 We spend $2,000,000+ per month on Meta only.

DO YOU WANT TO IMPACT THE HARDEST WORKING PEOPLE IN THE WORLD?

Then Jobber might be the place for you! We’re looking for a Senior Lifecycle Marketing Manager to be part of our Marketing department.



Jobber exists to help people in small businesses be successful. We work with small home service businesses, like your local plumbers, painters, and landscapers, to transform the way service is delivered through technology. With Jobber they can quote, schedule, invoice, and collect payments from their customers while providing an easy and professional customer experience. Running a small business today isn’t like it used to be—the way we consume and deliver service is changing rapidly, technology is evolving, and customers expect more. That’s why we put the power and flexibility in their hands to run their businesses how, where, and when they want!

Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration, and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work, Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, and more. Jobber has also been named on the Globe and Mail’s Canada’s Top Growing Companies list, and Deloitte Canada’s Technology Fast 50™, Enterprise Fast 15, and Technology Fast 500™ lists. With an Executive team that has over thirty years of industry experience of leading the way, we’ve come a long way from our first customer in 2011—but we’ve just scratched the surface of what we want to accomplish for our customers https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EkfZmHrRLx4&list=PLoktA_D-2UEnxMLfCe93bANKXVXd2bdN8&index=25.



The Team:

When it comes to telling the world about Jobber and moving new people through a funnel, Marketing is your department. They handle everything from spreading awareness, to answering “What’s Jobber?,” to getting new customers in the door, to turning those customers into Jobber advocates!

Lifecycle marketing is responsible for creating and advocating for best-in-class experiences that deliver the right message, to the right people, at the right time. We leverage automation and data to build highly personalized end-to-end experiences our customers want, need, and like.



The Role:

Reporting to the Acquisition Manager,  Lifecycle Marketing, the Senior Lifecycle Marketing Manager will be responsible for orchestrating our ideal customer experience. You will own and drive strategies for how we acquire, activate, retain, and expand users on all platforms. You will be accountable for enhancing our Lead Nurture efforts and creating experiences that are mutually beneficial to both customers and Jobber, ultimately ensuring we’re effectively capturing revenue.

You will partner cross-functionally to optimize our customer journey, including all associated customer communications. In addition, you will run experiments to explore and validate new strategies for how we can effectively move our customers through the funnel. You will represent Lifecycle Marketing across the organization and be a steward for your area of focus across the business.

Through your work with our Business Operations, Marketing, Sales, Success, Product, and Growth teams, you'll create great user experiences at scale and conduct experiments to discover what works.



The Senior Lifecycle Marketing Manager will:

 - Own the Leads portfolio end to end: the strategy, the programs, and the metrics for how leads are nurtured into trials and how trials convert into paying customers.

 - Own and extend Jobber’s AI-enriched lead journeys, using enrichment and orchestration tooling (currently Clay and n8n) to build customer profiles and route leads into personalized experiences based on intent.

 - Connect the lead experience to the trial experience so a customer sees one continuous, personalized journey from first touch through conversion, and work with Product on how that personalization carries into the app.

 - Run a test-and-learn program against lead-to-trial and trial-to-paid metrics: form hypotheses, design experiments, read the results honestly, and iterate until the number moves.

 - Decide where the portfolio’s time goes. Diagnose where leads and trials are being lost, size the opportunities, and make the case for what comes first and what waits.

 - Lead the acquisition pod that connects lifecycle with our outbound and demand generation partners, owning the plan and the handoffs between teams and keeping leadership informed.

 - Build what you design. Depending on capacity, you’ll configure journeys, write emails, and set up automation yourself alongside our Revenue Communications team.

 - Set the bar for the Lifecycle team: bring outside insight in, share what you learn, and raise how the practice works at Jobber.



To be successful, you should:

 - Have deep experience owning lead nurture and trial-to-paid conversion programs at a SaaS company, with results you can point to. B2B SaaS is the closest fit.

 - Have hands-on experience using AI tools to enrich customer data and personalize communications at scale, beyond drafting copy. You’ve built or configured enrichment, orchestration, or journey logic yourself and can say what it changed in your results.

 - Bring a test-and-learn posture to AI: you experiment with new tooling in your own workflow, can separate what works from what’s hype, and are comfortable in the weeds when the data is incomplete.

 - Have led integrated acquisition efforts across outbound, demand generation, product, and sales, owning the plan and the handoffs rather than executing the lifecycle piece of someone else’s.

 - Know the metrics behind nurture and conversion cold, and have moved them through experimentation and program iteration, not just reported on them.

 - Take full ownership of the outcomes tied to your KPIs, including when the data is imperfect. You find a way to measure, ship, and learn rather than wait for clean inputs.

 - Understand customer behaviour, barriers, and motivations from first-hand sources, and change the journey because of what you learn.

 - Operate with a high degree of autonomy. You set your own priorities, keep your manager informed without being asked, and flag risk early.

 - Push for better ways of doing things, and stay humble while you do it.



Location:

We believe great collaboration is intentional, and sometimes that means coming together in person to build, brainstorm, and connect. To support this, the role is open to candidates based in one of our hub cities: Edmonton, Toronto, Vancouver, or Kitchener-Waterloo.



Compensation:

At Jobber, we believe that compensation should be transparent, fair, and reflective of your experience and growth. This role has a minimum annual salary of $99,540, a midpoint of $142,200, and a maximum salary of $163,530, designed to show the progression from learning the ropes to truly excelling.

We design our compensation to reflect each new hire’s skills, experience against the complexity of the role, ensuring a fair and competitive salary. Our range is intentionally broad to support growth and long-term impact, with fully established hires typically starting around the midpoint. The higher end of the range is reserved for those who have demonstrated deep expertise and lasting contributions, while offers below the midpoint reflect strong potential with room to develop. This approach ensures that compensation aligns with both an individual’s current capabilities and their opportunity for future growth.

Base salary is just one part of a total compensation package that will include equity rewards, annual stipends for health and wellness, retirement savings matching, and an extended health package with fully paid premiums for body and mind. Your professional growth matters to us too! You’ll have access to a dedicated talent development program that includes career coaching and opportunities for career development.

We believe in transparency and open conversations about compensation. If you have any questions about our approach, we’re happy to discuss them throughout the hiring process!

What you can expect from Jobber:

 - A total compensation package that includes an extended health benefits package with fully paid premiums for both body and mind, matching in RRSP, TFSA or FHSA, and stock options.

 - A dedicated Talent Development team and access to coaching, learning, and leadership programs to help you grow your career, reach your goals, and unlock your full potential.

 - A unique opportunity to build, grow, and leave your impact on a $400-billion industry that has no dominant player...yet.

 - To work with a group of people who are humble, supportive, and give a sh*t about our customers.

We believe that diverse teams perform better and that fostering an inclusive work environment is a key part of growing a successful team. We welcome people of diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we are committed to working with applicants requesting accommodation at any stage of the hiring process.



A bit more about us:

Job by job, we’re transforming the way service is delivered. Your lawn care provider, home cleaning service, plumber or painter could use Jobber to better connect with their customers, save time in the office, invoice faster, and get paid! We’re bringing tens of thousands of people together with technology to deliver billions of dollars a year in services to happy customers. Jobber exists to help make these small businesses successful, and when they’re successful we all win!

 Company: WD Swim
 Location: 563 Edward Ave, Richmond Hill, ON L4C 9W7, Canada

 Pay: CA$22.00–CA$28.00 per hour
 Schedule: Must be available to work weekends

 About WD Swim
 WD Swim is a swim school serving families and swimmers across the Greater Toronto Area. We provide quality swimming lessons for children and adults of all ages and skill levels, with a strong commitment to safety, customer service, and creating a welcoming environment for our swimmers, families, and team members.
 We are looking for a friendly, organized, and detail-oriented Administrative Assistant & Front Desk Receptionist to support our daily operations and deliver an excellent experience for every family who interacts with our team.
 Position Overview
 The Administrative Assistant & Front Desk Receptionist is responsible for managing front desk operations, assisting customers, coordinating swim lesson registrations, and providing administrative support to management and staff.
 As the first point of contact for parents, swimmers, and visitors, you will play an important role in maintaining an organized, professional, and customer-focused environment. The ideal candidate is proactive, dependable, comfortable with computers, and able to manage multiple tasks while maintaining a high standard of service.
 Key Responsibilities
 Front Desk & Customer Service 
 Greet and assist parents, swimmers, visitors, and staff in a friendly and professional manner.
 Answer phone calls, respond to emails, and handle in-person inquiries regarding swim programs, lesson schedules, registrations, and facility policies.
 Provide accurate information about services, class availability, schedules, and general inquiries.
 Address customer concerns professionally and escalate issues to management when necessary.
 Maintain a welcoming, organized, and professional front desk environment.
 Administrative Support & Office Operations 
 Perform daily administrative duties, including data entry, document preparation, filing, scanning, and record maintenance.
 Maintain accurate and up-to-date customer information, registration records, and administrative files.
 Assist management with scheduling, internal communications, reports, and other administrative tasks.
 Coordinate information between parents, swim instructors, and management to support smooth daily operations.
 Monitor administrative tasks and follow up on outstanding inquiries or requests.
 Swim Lesson Registration & Payment Processing 
 Assist with swim lesson registrations, class bookings, schedule changes, cancellations, and customer check-ins.
 Process payments, issue receipts, and assist with basic billing and account inquiries.
 Update registration systems and customer records accurately.
 Communicate class schedules, program updates, and relevant announcements to parents and customers.
 Help ensure registration and front desk procedures are followed consistently.
 Operational Support 
 Follow company policies, procedures, and confidentiality requirements.
 Identify and report scheduling discrepancies, customer service concerns, and operational issues to management.
 Assist with general office coordination and other reasonable administrative duties as required.
 Why Join WD Swim?
 Competitive hourly compensation of CA$22.00–CA$28.00.
 Supportive and team-oriented work environment.
 Opportunities for professional development and career growth.
 Ongoing training and opportunities to develop administrative and customer service skills.
 The opportunity to contribute to a growing organization that supports swimming education and water safety.
 How to Apply
 If you are organized, dependable, and passionate about providing excellent customer service, we would love to hear from you.
 Apply today to join WD Swim and become an important part of the team supporting our swimmers, families, and daily operations.
 Qualifications & Requirements
 Previous experience in administrative support, front desk reception, customer service, or a similar role is preferred.
 Strong verbal and written communication skills.
 Excellent organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to multitask in a busy environment.
 Basic to intermediate computer skills, including email, spreadsheets, data entry, and scheduling or registration systems.
 Comfortable handling customer inquiries, processing payments, and maintaining accurate records.
 Professional, approachable, and customer-focused attitude.
 Ability to work independently while contributing positively to a team.
 Reliable, punctual, adaptable, and willing to take initiative.
 Ability to handle confidential customer and business information with discretion.
 Availability to work weekends is required. 
 Experience in a swim school, fitness centre, recreation facility, or other service-oriented business is an asset.

 GameSim is a game development studio that partners with clients to build games across PC/console and a range of art styles. We care about craftsmanship, collaboration, and shipping work we’re proud to put our names on. If you love building environments and believable spaces we’d like to meet you. Our headquarters is based in Orlando, FL!
 Talent Pipeline Posting Notice 
Please note that this posting is not tied to an immediate vacancy. We are proactively building a pipeline of qualified candidates in anticipation of potential hiring needs over the coming months. Applications will be reviewed and retained for future consideration as opportunities arise.
 We are seeking a Senior Lighting Artist to create high-quality real-time lighting and help guide lighting execution across GameSim projects.
 This is a hands-on senior role with leadership responsibilities. In addition to producing lighting work, you will review the work of other artists, provide clear direction and feedback, help organize lighting tasks, and ensure that scenes meet the visual and technical quality bar established by Art Direction and the client.
 You will collaborate closely with Art Directors, Environment Artists, Technical Artists, VFX Artists, Designers, Engineers, Producers, clients, and partner studios. You will help translate creative direction into practical lighting solutions that support mood, gameplay readability, environmental storytelling, narrative, and performance.
 This role may oversee the day-to-day work of other lighting artists or multidisciplinary artists contributing to lighting. It does not necessarily include formal people-management responsibilities, but it requires accountability for team output, effective mentorship, and the ability to raise concerns when work is at risk of missing quality, schedule, or technical expectations.
 What Success Looks Like
 Within your first 90 days, you will:
 Develop a clear understanding of the project’s visual direction, gameplay requirements, lighting pipeline, technical constraints, and production schedule.
 Build effective working relationships with Art Direction, Production, Technical Art, Environment Art, Design, Engineering, clients, and partner teams.
 Create polished lighting work that demonstrates the expected visual and technical quality bar.
 Take ownership of lighting for an assigned level, environment, sequence, or group of scenes.
 Review work from other artists and provide timely, actionable feedback that improves quality and consistency.
 Identify artistic, technical, or production risks early and work with project leadership to resolve them.
 Help the team deliver lighting work that meets milestone expectations for quality, performance, and completeness.
 Responsibilities
 Lighting Creation and Artistic Execution
 Create high-quality real-time lighting for gameplay environments, levels, cinematics, characters, and interactive sequences.
 Translate art direction, concept art, reference material, gameplay requirements, narrative goals, and client feedback into effective lighting solutions.
 Use lighting to establish mood, atmosphere, visual hierarchy, environmental storytelling, and player focus.
 Ensure lighting supports gameplay readability, navigation, combat visibility, character presentation, and important interactive elements.
 Develop and refine exposure, color, contrast, fog, atmosphere, reflections, shadows, emissive response, color grading, and post-processing.
 Create lighting for a range of visual styles, including realistic, stylized, cinematic, and highly art-directed projects.
 Maintain consistency across connected environments, gameplay spaces, cinematics, times of day, weather conditions, and lighting scenarios.
 Bring assigned scenes to final quality while meeting technical requirements and production deadlines.
 Leadership and Quality Oversight
 Oversee lighting work for an assigned area of the project, such as a level, world region, sequence, feature, or milestone.
 Review the work of lighting artists and other contributors whose work affects the final lighting result.
 Provide clear, constructive, and actionable feedback through live reviews, written notes, paintovers, reference boards, documentation, and in-engine examples.
 Ensure lighting work follows the visual direction, technical standards, and quality expectations established by Art Direction and the client.
 Help artists understand priorities, expected outcomes, acceptance criteria, and the level of polish required for each milestone.
 Track the visual progress of assigned lighting work and identify scenes that require additional support, revision, or escalation.
 Verify that feedback has been addressed and that completed work meets the established quality bar before submission.
 Mentor junior and mid-level artists in lighting fundamentals, technical execution, scene organization, optimization, and production practices.
 Lead by example through strong artistic execution, professional communication, reliable follow-through, and practical problem-solving.
 Help resolve differing artistic opinions by referring decisions back to approved visual targets, gameplay needs, technical constraints, and project priorities.
 Escalate unresolved quality, scope, staffing, scheduling, or technical risks to the appropriate project leads.
 Planning and Production Support
 Work with Art Direction and Production to break down lighting goals into clear tasks, priorities, estimates, and milestone deliverables.
 Help assess lighting scope, scene complexity, dependencies, and production risks.
 Support task assignment based on artist strengths, project priorities, and schedule needs.
 Provide progress updates and communicate when work is likely to miss visual, technical, or scheduling expectations.
 Participate in daily reviews, milestone evaluations, client reviews, and project-planning discussions.
 Help prepare lighting work for internal reviews, client presentations, milestone submissions, and final delivery.
 Balance hands-on production responsibilities with review, mentorship, troubleshooting, and team support.
 Adapt plans and priorities when creative direction, production scope, technical requirements, or client feedback changes.
 Technical and Pipeline Responsibilities
 Partner with Technical Art and Engineering to ensure lighting solutions are visually effective, technically stable, and appropriate for the target platform.
 Work within established budgets for frame rate, dynamic lights, shadows, volumetrics, reflections, global illumination, memory, and scalability.
 Diagnose and resolve issues involving exposure, shadow artifacts, light leaking, reflections, global illumination, volumetrics, bake quality, material response, and post-processing.
 Determine when to use dynamic, baked, stationary, or hybrid lighting approaches based on project requirements.
 Profile lighting work and make informed visual tradeoffs to meet performance requirements.
 Validate lighting across relevant gameplay cameras, display settings, hardware targets, times of day, weather states, and scalability levels.
 Help develop and maintain reusable lighting setups, templates, documentation, validation processes, and best practices.
 Identify workflow inefficiencies and recommend practical improvements to Art Direction, Technical Art, or Production.
 Follow project standards for scene organization, naming conventions, source control, documentation, and asset integration.
 Cross-Discipline Collaboration
 Collaborate with Environment Art to ensure geometry, materials, composition, and set dressing support the intended lighting.
 Partner with VFX to integrate fog, particles, weather, fire, emissive effects, and atmospheric elements.
 Work with Design to ensure lighting supports navigation, player guidance, combat readability, objectives, and interactive systems.
 Coordinate with Character Art and Animation to maintain readable and appealing character presentation in gameplay and cinematics.
 Partner with Cinematics teams on shot composition, continuity, exposure, character lighting, and narrative focus.
 Communicate artistic and technical tradeoffs clearly to both creative and non-creative stakeholders.
 Work effectively with distributed teams, partner studios, external vendors, and clients across different time zones.
 Requirements
 Professional experience creating lighting for games, real-time projects, or a closely related field.
 At least one shipped game or comparable professional real-time project.
 A portfolio or reel demonstrating high-quality real-time lighting.
 Strong understanding of lighting fundamentals, including value, color, contrast, composition, visual hierarchy, atmosphere, exposure, shadow, and material response.
 Experience lighting gameplay environments and interactive real-time scenes.
 Strong understanding of how lighting supports mood, gameplay readability, navigation, environmental storytelling, and player focus.
 Professional experience using Unreal Engine or another modern real-time engine.
 Experience with dynamic and baked lighting, global illumination, reflections, volumetrics, exposure, color grading, and post-processing.
 Working knowledge of physically based rendering, material response, tone mapping, and high-dynamic-range lighting.
 Understanding of real-time lighting optimization, including light cost, shadow complexity, volumetrics, reflections, memory, scalability, and platform constraints.
 Experience taking ownership of lighting for a level, scene, sequence, environment, or comparable area of production.
 Experience reviewing the work of other artists and providing clear, actionable feedback.
 Ability to identify when work does not meet the established quality bar and communicate what is required to improve it.
 Demonstrated ability to balance artistic quality, technical limitations, production scope, and schedule requirements.
 Ability to solve artistic and technical problems with limited supervision.
 Strong written, verbal, presentation, and interpersonal communication skills.
 Experience collaborating with Art Direction, Environment Art, Technical Art, VFX, Design, Engineering, Production, or Cinematics.
 Ability to organize priorities, communicate risks, and follow work through to completion.
 Ability to adapt to different projects, visual styles, engines, pipelines, platforms, and client expectations.
 Comfort participating in internal and client-facing art reviews.
 Tools and Technical Experience
 Candidates should have strong experience with a professional real-time lighting toolset. This may include:
 Unreal Engine 5 or another modern real-time engine
 Lumen or comparable real-time global-illumination systems
 GPU Lightmass, CPU Lightmass, or comparable baked-lighting systems
 Real-time profiling, visualization, and debugging tools
 Photoshop or comparable image-editing software
 DaVinci Resolve, Nuke, After Effects, or comparable color and compositing tools
 Maya, Blender, 3ds Max, or another 3D content-creation package
 Perforce or another production source-control system
 Jira, Confluence, Miro, or comparable planning and documentation tools
 Expertise with every listed application is not required. We are primarily interested in candidates who demonstrate strong lighting fundamentals, production judgment, technical adaptability, and the ability to learn project-specific tools.
 Preferred Qualifications
 Experience working in co-development, outsourcing, consulting, or work-for-hire game production.
 Experience contributing to AAA PC or console titles.
 Experience working across both realistic and stylized visual pipelines.
 Previous experience acting as a lighting point person, feature owner, task lead, or senior reviewer.
 Experience coordinating the work of other artists without formal management authority.
 Experience working with remote teams, partner studios, or external vendors.
 Experience owning the lighting for a level, biome, world region, cinematic sequence, or major gameplay feature.
 Advanced Unreal Engine knowledge, including Lumen, Nanite, Virtual Shadow Maps, volumetric fog, reflection systems, exposure controls, post-process volumes, lighting channels, and scalability settings.
 Experience with dynamic time-of-day systems, weather systems, destructible environments, or changing gameplay states.
 Experience lighting cinematics, characters, dialogue scenes, or scripted sequences in a real-time engine.
 Knowledge of cinematography, photography, film lighting, camera exposure, lens behavior, and color science.
 Experience with HDR displays, tone mapping, platform calibration, accessibility considerations, or multiple display formats.
 Familiarity with rendering pipelines, shader behavior, material development, and image-based lighting.
 Familiarity with Blueprints, Python, editor scripting, automation, or technical-art workflows.
 Experience creating lighting documentation, templates, validation tools, or review processes.
 Experience participating in estimates, staffing discussions, hiring reviews, portfolio evaluations, or art tests.
 Portfolio Requirements
 Your portfolio or reel should demonstrate:
 High-quality real-time lighting with strong composition, mood, color, contrast, readability, atmosphere, and scene cohesion.
 Work presented in a commercial, proprietary, or modern real-time engine.
 Clear explanations of your individual contribution, responsibilities, workflow, and production decisions.
 Gameplay lighting that guides attention, supports navigation, and reinforces the intended player experience.
 Effective integration between lighting, environments, materials, VFX, atmosphere, characters, and post-processing.
 An understanding of optimization, scalability, technical limitations, and production constraints.
 Examples showing ownership of lighting from initial direction or blockout through final delivery.
 The ability to work from concept art, reference, environment blockouts, narrative direction, gameplay requirements, or incomplete creative direction.
 Adaptability across different projects, genres, visual styles, or lighting conditions.
 We also encourage applicants to include:
 Day and night treatments of the same environment.
 Dynamic and baked lighting examples.
 Lighting created for different gameplay states, weather conditions, or times of day.
 Before-and-after comparisons showing how lighting improved readability, mood, composition, or performance.
 Examples of scenes that were reviewed or completed under your guidance, with your responsibilities clearly explained.
 Lighting guides, benchmark scenes, review notes, color scripts, documentation, or templates created for other artists.
 Please clearly identify your individual contribution to collaborative work.
 How to Apply
 A resume and portfolio or reel link are required.
 Please include shipped-game credits or comparable professional project experience where applicable. Candidates may be asked to participate in a portfolio review, technical discussion, leadership interview, or art assessment as part of the selection process.

About Citylitics Inc. 
Citylitics delivers predictive intelligence on where, how, and why infrastructure investments will occur across North America.
 Infrastructure includes the foundational systems that shape our quality of life: water, transportation, transit, roads and highways, broadband, and power. It represents a multi-trillion-dollar market and a 20+ year megatrend in North America.
 Citylitics transforms millions of documents across more than 40,000 cities, utilities, and public agencies into real-time market signals and high-value sales intelligence. Leading infrastructure vendors, engineering firms, and construction companies use the platform to identify and pre-position for major infrastructure opportunities earlier, helping them build relationships, shape project priorities, and influence scope before projects move to formal procurement. 
 Citylitics combines a network of AI agents, fine-tuned models, a proprietary infrastructure signals graph, and daily human-in-the-loop quality assurance workflows to deliver highly nuanced and reliable sales intelligence. The platform integrates seamlessly with CRMs, ERPs, and data lakes, embedding actionable insights directly into sales workflows so teams can prioritize the right pursuits and build stronger pipelines.
 Our mission is to improve how infrastructure investments get made so critical needs can be addressed earlier and communities benefit from stronger, more resilient infrastructure.
 Join Citylitics to work in a meaningful industry that will matter for decades to come while helping grow a company at the forefront of applied AI. We operate with a Results-Driven Mentality and a commitment to Raise The Bar, in a collaborative environment where Teamwork Makes the Dream Work as we tackle big challenges and celebrate wins together.
 Who Are We Looking For? 
 We're looking for a skilled and enthusiastic Data Engineer to join our growing team! We're a close-knit group building and maintaining mission-critical data products, and we need someone who can hit the ground running.
 This role requires a strong command of data engineering best practices, a track record with orchestration and data warehouses, and hands-on experience shipping LLM and agentic workflows to production. You'll own the design, build, and operation of production data pipelines that use AI to power customer-facing solutions. You'll work with technologies we already use, including GCP services like Cloud Composer, Cloud SQL, BigQuery, and Vertex AI.
 Beyond the technical skills, we value collaboration, sound engineering judgment, and the ability to adapt as AI tooling changes fast. If you're passionate about data, have put AI into production and want to do more of it, and are excited by impactful projects, we encourage you to apply.
 This is a hybrid role based out of Citylitics’ Toronto office and requires 3+ days in-office per week. 
 What Will You Accomplish? / How You Will Make An Immediate Impact: 
 Pipeline Orchestration: Lead the development of highly performant, reliable, and maintainable pipelines using Airflow and BigQuery, from architecture and design through testing, deployment, monitoring, and maintenance. You'll make design decisions independently and own the systems you build.
 Data Modeling & Dashboards: Partner with data analysts and stakeholders to define requirements and design scalable data models and applications. You'll own data products end to end, from the pipelines and models through the backend APIs to the customer-facing dashboards and apps built on them.
 AI & Agentic Workflows: Design and operate pipelines that use LLMs and agents to turn raw documents into structured, useful data. This includes prompt and context design, tool and function calling, embeddings and retrieval, structured outputs, and production concerns like retries, idempotency, cost, and latency. You'll also own evaluation datasets, LLM-as-judge and rule-based QA checks, and benchmarks that turn results into clear decisions about models, prompts, and architecture.
 Continuous Improvement: Drive the ongoing improvement of our data infrastructure and processes, including evaluating and introducing new technologies and best practices. We're an AI-first team that uses coding agents like Claude Code daily for development, debugging, review, and documentation, and we're looking for someone who can help shape how we push that further.
 Other duties as assigned 
 Proficiency in Python and SQL.
 Proven experience (3+ years) working as a Data Engineer or Software Engineer in a cloud environment.
 Experience building production data pipelines with an orchestrator like Airflow/Cloud Composer and a data warehouse like BigQuery.
 Solid grasp of data engineering fundamentals: data modeling, ETL/ELT, and building idempotent, reliable pipelines.
 Experience shipping LLM-powered features or pipelines to production with LLM APIs (e.g., Gemini, Claude, OpenAI): prompting, structured outputs, and tool/function calling.
 Working knowledge of agent patterns (tool use, multi-step workflows, retrieval/RAG, MCP) and their production tradeoffs, such as cost, latency, and failure modes.
 Daily, fluent use of AI coding agents (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor) in your workflow, with the judgment to review and verify what they produce.
 Experience with Git, CI/CD, and cloud platforms (GCP preferred).
 Experience building data apps or dashboards end to end, including a backend API and a frontend (e.g., React, TypeScript), is a plus.
 Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently on ambiguous problems.
 Excellent communication and collaboration skills. You'll be working closely with analysts, product, and other stakeholders.
 Vacancy Status: This position is for an existing and active vacancy that the company is currently seeking to fill.
 What’s in it for you? 
 Make real-world impact: Influence positive change across one of the biggest societal challenges of our generation: building and maintaining sustainable public infrastructure.
 Sell a genuinely differentiated platform: You’ll represent a disruptive, data-driven solution with a compelling value proposition in a market that is eager to engage.
 Operate at the intersection of infrastructure, scale-up, and data science: We live where infrastructure meets AI and advanced data. There is no other team like ours in Toronto.
 Move fast, learn faster: There’s no corporate bureaucracy here. You’ll accomplish more in a few months than you would in years at a large, entrenched technology company.
 Be empowered by data and AI: We believe Data and AI will play an outsized role in the future of sales and decision-making. Every CityZen has access to generative AI tools and our full data universe to enhance productivity and encourage experimentation.
 Grow with intention: We invest deeply in our people through in-role coaching, skill-based development, and clear internal promotion pathways.
 Win as a team: We work hard, we support one another, and we celebrate progress along the way. We’re serious about solving infrastructure and just as serious about enjoying the journey together.

 Role Introduction 
 The Site Technical Advisor (Turbine and Generator) serves as the dedicated on-site technical specialist responsible for supporting the installation and commissioning of hydroelectric projects. This critical role ensures that all mechanical and associated site works are executed safely, to the highest quality standards, on schedule, and within budget, while strictly adhering to design specifications and regulatory requirements.
 Responsibilities 
   Environment, Health, and Safety (EHS): 
 Ensure EHS compliance, evaluate tasks for worker hazards, and confirm controls are active. Stop work if risks are insufficiently mitigated.
 Promote a strong safety culture and ensure technical work complies with EHS requirements, including participation in risk assessments and Job Safety Analyses (JSAs) for high-risk activities (heavy lifts, confined spaces, hot work, working at heights, energized work).
 Support environmental protection measures and regulatory compliance during construction and commissioning.
 Planning and Construction Coordination: 
 Work closely with the Site Manager to plan, sequence, and provide technical inputs to construction schedules and critical path activities.
 Act as the primary on-site technical point of contact for design engineers, project managers, methods engineers, subcontractors, and customer representatives.
 Participate in technical meetings, design clarifications, change management discussions, and coordinate with specialized subcontractors.
