 Provide day-to-day technical guidance, expertise, and leadership to on-site construction and labor teams.
 Closely monitor critical installation processes, such as turbine/generator alignment, bearing installation, shaft coupling, and critical lifts.
 Perform skilled technical duties involving shaft line alignment, bearing settings, precision mechanical tools, measurements, and on-site machining tools.
 Review and interpret engineering drawings, manuals, and specifications to verify adherence to design, codes, standards, and OEM requirements.
   Quality, Testing, and Project Closeout: 
 Participate in inspections and critical quality checks (alignment, welding, grouting) and report any quality issues or non-conformities per the site quality plan.
 Support the resolution of technical non-conformances and punch list items.
 Review and validate test results, support the preparation of as-built documentation, and assist with O&M handover packages.
 Lead or contribute to root cause analyses for construction issues, recommend technical solutions/field changes, and capture lessons learned.
 Qualifications and Skills 
 Education: Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, electrical, or civil engineering (or a related technical discipline). An equivalent technical diploma with substantial hydro or power plant construction experience will be considered.
   Experience: 
 Minimum of 5 years of prior hydroelectric generator experience, preferably in a supervisory capacity.
 Minimum of 5 years of experience in the mechanical installation of shaft lines, turbines, or generators.
 Strong working knowledge of hydroelectric plant systems and structures; ability to read and interpret manuals, drawings, plans, and specifications.
   Interpersonal and Professional Skills 
 Demonstrated ability to lead, motivate, and empower staff while working effectively under pressure.
 Strong problem-solving, decision-making, and field-environment judgment.
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with good computer skills and MS Office knowledge.
 Proactive attitude toward safety and the ability to build and maintain effective working relationships across multi-disciplinary teams.

 Relocation Assistance Provided: No

 Small print here ⇒ We’re an eCommerce company. So, we want you to have eCommerce experience. Lots of it. So if you don’t love digital marketing the way cats love cream, you probably shouldn’t read any further. 
 Still here? Okay then…
 This job will give you ALL the feels:
 At AlgaeCal, we’re driven by a single idea. To end the fear of bone loss. In the United States, an estimated 54 million people have low bone density. 
 The good news? AlgaeCal has the world’s only clinically-backed natural solution to this problem. We give hope to everyone worried about bone loss. If that excites you, you’ll find no better place to continue your career than at AlgaeCal. 
 This job might be for you if you’ve got…
 2+ years of marketing leadership experience planning and executing D2C campaigns in an eCommerce environment. You’ve led campaigns from the first messy idea through briefing, approvals, launch, optimization, reporting, and “okay, what did we learn?” You know campaigns don’t magically happen because someone made a promo calendar. They happen because someone owns the moving parts.
 A track record of managing six-figure monthly marketing budgets. You've worked with substantial media investments, understand how budget allocation impacts overall business performance, and know that maximizing profit matters more than simply maximizing spend.
 A Yoda-like ability to make strategic, data-driven decisions. When we look at your resume, we’ll see proof that you know how to turn campaign performance data into smart decisions. CPA, ROAS, revenue, customer segments, contribution margin, EBITDA - these numbers don’t make your eyes glaze over. They make your brain start whirring.
 A full-funnel brain that sees the whole customer journey. Paid media, email, ecommerce, loyalty, organic social, affiliates, influencers, customer service, marketplaces - you understand these channels don’t live in separate little kingdoms. They all touch the same customer. And if the journey feels disjointed, confusing, repetitive, or poorly timed, performance suffers.
 Strategy that converts like a tent revival. You’ve planned campaigns that engage, educate, and motivate people to take action. You understand offer strategy, timing, landing pages, upsells, cross-sells, bundles, coupons, discount logic, and the tiny campaign mechanics that can quietly make or break revenue. You know when evergreen ads, emails, popups, organic posts, or automations need to pause, shift, suppress, or get out of the way so a live campaign can do its job.
 A brain the size of a small planet! In this role, you’ll need to think imaginatively and act strategically. You’ll balance company priorities, finance approvals, product logistics, creative capacity, compliance, customer service needs, and channel constraints without melting into a puddle.
 A results-driven approach to paid media and campaign budget. You’ve worked closely with Paid Media teams, helped allocate spend across campaigns, and know how to look beyond surface-level ROAS. Revenue is nice. Profitability is nicer. You understand unit economics, contribution margin, and why a campaign can look good in one dashboard and less thrilling in another.
 A track record of leadership, mentorship, and cross-functional coordination. You’ve worked with channel owners, project managers, analysts, creatives, and senior leaders to get campaigns out the door without everyone needing therapy afterward. You guide, influence, pitch, negotiate, and push back when needed - without turning into a tiny workplace dictator.
 The ability to put on the Customer Hat at all times. You think through what a new prospect sees, what a returning customer receives, how reward points affect the offer, what happens if someone talks to Customer Service, and whether the whole experience actually makes sense to a real human being.
 Experience designing and executing customer journeys. From first click to final purchase, from campaign email to landing page, from retargeting ad to checkout, from BAU content to live promo, you know how to make every touchpoint feel connected, intentional, and easy to follow.
 A thick portfolio that demonstrates your mastery of all-things eCommerce. Sorry, but if you have to Google what a heatmap is, don’t know why site speed matters, or think an A/B test is just “trying a different headline,” this probably isn’t the job for you.
 A detective’s eye for revenue leakage. Coupon abuse, conflicting emails, poorly timed popups, expired offers, unclear bundles, bad suppression logic, clunky checkout journeys, ads running to the wrong page - you can spot the problems before they quietly drain sales.
 An encyclopedic knowledge of today’s martech, adtech, attribution, and analytics landscape. You don’t blindly trust one dashboard because it has a pretty graph. You understand tools like Triple Whale and GA4 can disagree, and you know how to contextualize performance instead of taking any single source as gospel.
 A strong grasp of testing strategy. A/B testing, multivariate testing, UX tests, offer tests, funnel tests, creative tests - you know how to plan tests that align with bigger roadmaps instead of throwing spaghetti at a wall and calling it “experimentation.”
 A solid understanding of UI/UX. This isn’t essential, but it’s a definite plus. You don’t need to be a designer, but you should understand how UX and UI choices affect customer behavior, conversion, trust, and campaign performance. And yes, we might swoon if you have it.
 A healthy respect for compliance, claims, and disclaimers. We work in the health space, which means “close enough” is not close enough. You’ll need to understand marketing claims, product basics, customer service considerations, and legal disclaimers well enough to keep campaigns accurate, compliant, and trustworthy.
 Now, time to be honest: is this really you? If you’re nodding your head and feeling that flutter of excitement, then we can’t wait to meet you.
 Other Qualities You’ll Need 
 At AlgaeCal, we’re going to insist that you have these 3 qualities:
 You’re humble–you put the team and others’ needs ahead of your own
 You’re hungry to learn more
 You’re people smart–in the sense that you’re a great teammate

 What Will You Earn?

 Monthly team events and activities

 How To Apply

ABOUT SOLINK

At Solink, our mission is to safeguard what matters most. We provide businesses with the tools to know sooner and act faster by transforming video security into real-time operational insights.

Our cloud-based platform integrates seamlessly with your existing cameras and systems, turning them into intelligent sensors that detect and interpret key moments. This empowers teams to make data-driven decisions, enhance security, and improve operational efficiency.

Trusted by over 35,000 locations across 60+ countries - including brands like McDonald’s and JYSK - Solink delivers clarity when it counts. Our solutions help businesses reduce shrink, optimize performance, and respond proactively to potential threats.

We're growing rapidly, earning industry recognition, and scaling with purpose. We’ve been recognized by Deloitte’s Fast 50™ and Fast 500™, Business Intelligence Group, and as one of Ottawa’s Best Places to Work. And we’re just getting started!




THE ROLE

As Director, Deployment Operations, you'll own Solink's end-to-end sales-to-deployment operating model, from the moment a deal closes to the point a customer is live, supported and generating recurring revenue. Our Deployment function has grown in scale, complexity and strategic importance, and this role exists to lead it into its next chapter.

You'll lead a team across three focus areas: Deployment Execution, Optimization & Automation, and Operations Enablement. You'll be accountable for the overall function and driving major automation and process-improvement initiatives and partnering with senior leaders across the organization to improve planning, quality, scalability and accountability.

This is an opportunity for an operations leader who's energized by building systems that scale, raising the bar on execution and connecting operational performance directly to ARR growth.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own the sales-to-deployment operating model: Define and continuously improve how work flows from Sales through Deployment to Support, including handoffs, planning, capacity, quality standards and accountability at every stage.

 - Lead and develop a high-performing leadership team: Lead Managers across Deployment Execution, Optimization & Automation, and Enablement & Cross-Functional. Set clear goals, coach for growth and build a leadership bench that can scale with the business.

 - Drive operational transformation: Lead major automation, tooling and process-improvement initiatives that increase throughput, reduce cycle time and improve the customer deployment experience.

 - Deliver on ARR: Ensure deployments are executed on time and at quality so that contracted revenue converts to recurring revenue predictably. Own the metrics, forecasting and reporting that connect operations to financial outcomes.

 - Partner across the organization: Work closely with senior leaders in Sales, Customer Success, Support, Product and Finance to align on planning, resolve cross-functional friction and make Deployment a strategic lever for the business.

 - Establish governance and operational rigour: Set the standards, SOPs, KPIs and reporting cadence that give leadership clear visibility into deployment health, capacity and risk.

 - Oversee partner and field strategy: Guide how Solink works with installation partners and field resources, including partner enablement, performance management and relationship health.

 - Serve as the senior escalation point: Own resolution of high-impact customer and operational escalations, and turn recurring issues into systemic fixes.




ROLE EXPECTATIONS

This is an M4 level role. At Solink, individuals at this level serve as a strategic advisor within a department, who is confident acting as their executive leader’s right hand within their functional area and is able to set cross-functional direction in collaboration with departments within the organization.



In this role, you'll be expected to:

 - Set the vision and multi-quarter roadmap for the Deployment function and translate it into clear priorities for your managers.

 - Operate with a high degree of autonomy, making decisions that shape how the function runs and how it interacts with the rest of the business.

 - Influence senior stakeholders across functions, building alignment on shared goals, processes and trade-offs.

 - Balance near-term delivery with long-term investment in automation, tooling and scalability.

 - Build a culture of ownership, quality and continuous improvement across the Deployment team.

What success looks like:

 - Deployment cycle times, on-time delivery and quality metrics improve measurably, and ARR from new deals is realized faster and more predictably.

 - Key automation and process-improvement initiatives are delivered, reducing manual effort and allowing the function to scale without proportional headcount growth.

 - Sales, Deployment, Support and other partners operate from a shared planning model with clear handoffs, visible accountability and fewer escalations.


WHAT YOU BRING

 - 8+ years in operations, deployment, implementation or professional services, including 3+ years leading managers or multi-team functions.

 - A proven track record of designing and scaling an end-to-end operating model in a high-growth B2B technology, SaaS or hardware-enabled services environment.

 - Demonstrated success leading process-improvement and automation initiatives with measurable impact on efficiency, quality or revenue.

 - Strong analytical and business acumen, with experience owning KPIs, capacity planning and operational reporting tied to financial outcomes such as ARR.

 - Excellent cross-functional leadership and communication skills, with the credibility to influence senior leaders and drive alignment.

Nice-to-Have:

 - Experience in physical security, video surveillance, IoT or other field-deployed technology.

 - Experience managing installation partner or channel networks across multiple regions.

 - Familiarity with operations tooling and automation platforms (e.g., Salesforce, HubSpot, NetSuite, Asana, Jira, n8n or similar).

 - Background in Lean, Six Sigma or other formal continuous-improvement methodologies.




SECURITY REQUIREMENTS

 - Candidates must undergo a criminal records check upon hire;

 - Be a Canadian Citizen (dual citizens included), or eligible to work in Canada;

 - Be willing to comply with Solink’s own security policies and standards.


COMPENSATION

We determine compensation based on the experience, skills, and impact you bring to the role.

For this position, we are hiring within the Proficient range. OUR VALUES

 - Win with TEAM – No egos. Just outcomes, built together.

WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!







ROLE OVERVIEW

We're seeking a senior product leader to own Cohere's Inference as a Service business end to end. The product is sovereign, self-serve inference: a mid-market or enterprise buyer picks a model, a region and a GPU size, and is running the same afternoon with no procurement cycle and no infrastructure of their own. You'll decide which open-weights and first-party models we serve, in which regions and on which hardware, set the rate card they sell at, and carry the revenue and margin that follow from those calls. You own the platform around that endpoint as well, from the console and dashboards a customer administers their deployment through to the catalog of first-party and third-party models behind it.

You'll set the strategy and run the execution, which means choosing where to spend across serving efficiency, the self-serve console and regional capacity when all three want the same budget, and shipping the deployment framework that removes infrastructure barriers while holding the line on data residency, compliance and operational confidence. You'll do that across engineering, serving, finance, legal and GTM without formal authority over most of it, and you'll be accountable for the outcome rather than for the roadmap.

The timing is most of the opportunity. Every serious company is deciding where its models will run and what it costs to keep them running, serving demand is climbing faster than anyone can rack hardware for it, and very few of those buyers are willing to hand their data to an operator who can read it. We are starting this business from a standing start, with the models, the silicon and the encryption already in place and almost no one else able to offer the combination. You would be taking a product to market in the window where that advantage is still ours, building one of Cohere's major revenue lines from its first customer onward, and shaping how a generation of companies buys AI it can actually trust.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own the P&L for Inference as a Service: carry the revenue number, set the rate card, and keep blended margin above the floor as the catalog and the fleet grow.

 - Own the inference platform itself: the console and dashboards where customers see usage, spend, API keys, access control and attestation, and the value-add tooling that makes a managed endpoint worth more than a raw one.

 - Own the model inventory across first-party and third-party models: what enters the catalog, how it is grouped by provenance, what it is priced at, and when something is quantised, replaced or retired.

 - Set the roadmap and the investment case across serving efficiency, the self-serve surface and regional capacity, and make the call when those three compete for the same budget.

 - Build the commercial motion with GTM from the ground up: self-serve acquisition for the mid-market, a sales-led motion for enterprise, and the partnerships that monetise capacity we would otherwise leave idle.

 - Stay close to the market: talk to customers and developers about integration friction and unmet needs, track competitor pricing, catalogs and launches, and follow where models and hardware are heading, then turn that into a clear view of where we should place our bets and what it would take to win.

 - Define the metrics that tell us whether this is a business, including revenue, margin, win rate, time to first token and self-serve share, and lead the work that moves them.

 - Partner with engineering, research, legal, finance, technical writing and developer relations to ship the platform and clear the licensing, pricing and capacity decisions behind it.

 - Represent the business to the executive team with a recommendation, the evidence behind it and the trade-off it implies.




REQUIREMENTS

 - 10+ years of product management experience, including meaningful time owning a B2B infrastructure or platform product at the scope of a business rather than a feature area.

 - Experience operating in a GM-like capacity: you have carried a revenue line or a P&L, set pricing, and been held to margin as well as to shipping.

 - Background at a neocloud such as Together AI, Baseten or Fireworks, or at a hyperscaler such as AWS, Azure, OCI or Google Cloud, with a working view of how inference capacity is priced, packaged and sold, and a point of view on where the segment goes next.

 - A track record of thinking about infrastructure as a product, with the ability to translate system-level capabilities into clearly differentiated, customer-facing features.

 - Entrepreneurial, with experience taking a new product to market and building the commercial motion around it rather than inheriting one.

 - Experience with deployment models such as multi-tenant and dedicated infrastructure, and ownership across the full product lifecycle, from problem definition through launch, iteration and eventual migration or deprecation.

 - Analytical by default: you define success metrics before you build, instrument thoughtfully, and use data alongside qualitative feedback to make decisions.

 - Able to set direction and earn alignment across engineering, infrastructure, finance, legal and GTM without formal authority, and to put a clear recommendation and its trade-offs in front of an executive audience.




NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Experience owning a model serving or inference platform, including self-serve infrastructure and metered inference offerings.

 - Exposure to data residency, sovereignty, or regional compliance requirements as they apply to AI or cloud infrastructure products, particularly in the inference-as-a-service context.

 - Familiarity with the AI developer ecosystem and open standards, including orchestration frameworks such as LangChain and LlamaIndex, model serving frameworks such as vLLM, and an awareness of de facto interoperability standards and how they shape developer adoption and integration patterns for inference workloads.

 - Experience with GPU infrastructure and cloud deployment models across both neocloud and hyperscaler environments.




FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

 - Annual enrichment benefits:
   
   Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.
   
   Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

 - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

 - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.




HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

 How you will make an impact 
 As a member of Ciena’s Emergency Response Team (ERT), you will play a critical role in restoring customer networks during high-severity incidents involving Ciena’s Coherent Packet Optical (CPO) portfolio, including the 6500, RLS, and Waveserver platforms. You will apply your optical networking expertise, analytical troubleshooting skills, and incident management experience to resolve complex network issues, minimize service disruption, and deliver exceptional customer outcomes.
 Drive critical incident recovery: Take ownership of high-severity customer incidents, including Severity 1 and Severity 2 events, and lead troubleshooting efforts to restore services within established recovery objectives.
 Troubleshoot complex optical networks: Investigate and resolve service-impacting issues across optical transport networks, using system alarms, logs, performance data, topology information, and other diagnostic tools to isolate faults and determine recovery actions.
 Restore customer services: Develop and execute structured recovery strategies, assess potential service impacts, and coordinate technical activities to achieve timely and effective service restoration.
 Engage directly with customers: Communicate technical findings, recovery plans, progress updates, and next steps clearly throughout critical incidents, maintaining customer confidence during high-pressure situations.
 Collaborate across technical teams: Work with product engineering, development, global technical support, and other subject matter experts to resolve complex problems and investigate potential product defects.
 Prepare root cause analysis: Develop interim root cause analysis reports, documenting incident timelines, technical findings, recovery actions, contributing factors, and outstanding investigations.
 Maintain technical documentation: Accurately record troubleshooting activities, diagnostic evidence, customer communications, and resolution details to support effective incident management and knowledge sharing.
 Improve recovery effectiveness: Participate in post-incident reviews, lessons learned, knowledge management, and continuous improvement initiatives that strengthen technical readiness and reduce recovery times.

 Optical networking experience: 4+ years of experience in optical transport, telecommunications, network engineering, or technical support for carrier-grade networking equipment.
 Technical troubleshooting: Demonstrated experience diagnosing complex network or service issues in production environments, using alarms, logs, performance metrics, network topology, and other diagnostic information.
 Network recovery: Ability to analyze service-impacting failures, develop effective troubleshooting strategies, and drive restoration activities in environments with stringent availability and recovery requirements.
 Optical transport fundamentals: Strong understanding of optical transport networks and relevant technologies, such as DWDM, coherent optics, wavelength services, optical performance monitoring, or related transport technologies.
 Incident ownership: Ability to manage critical technical issues from initial investigation through service restoration, prioritizing actions and coordinating the appropriate technical resources.
 Customer engagement: Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical problems, recovery strategies, and incident status to customers and internal stakeholders.
 Technical documentation: Experience documenting technical investigations, troubleshooting procedures, and incident findings. The ability to produce clear, structured technical reports is essential.
 Collaboration and judgment: Ability to work independently, make sound technical decisions under pressure, and collaborate effectively with geographically distributed teams.
 On-call availability: Willingness to participate in a scheduled rotational on-call model, including weekend coverage (once every 4–5 weeks).

 Hands-on experience with Ciena optical networking platforms, particularly the 6500, RLS, or Waveserver product families.
 Experience supporting optical transport equipment from other telecommunications vendors, such as Nokia, Infinera, Cisco, or equivalent optical networking platforms.
 Advanced knowledge of DWDM, coherent optical transmission, wavelength provisioning, optical power levels, signal quality, and optical performance troubleshooting.

 A continuous improvement mindset, with an interest in improving troubleshooting effectiveness, incident recovery processes, and customer experience through data-driven analysis and product feedback.

 Job Description
 Location: Remote — United States, Canada, or United Kingdom only
 Compensation: $145,000–$180,000 OTE
 ABOUT TRIVIUM
 Trivium Group is an Inc. 5000-ranked, Clutch Award-winning Amazon growth agency. We manage millions in ad spend and help brands scale profitably on the world's most competitive marketplace. Our closers don't take orders — they own the number. This is a small, high-performing team.
 THE ROLE
 This is a full sales cycle seat, not a closer-only seat.
 Qualified leads come to you. Demand is inbound heavy, generated through our own paid marketing across Amazon, Meta and Google, so warm leads land on your calendar — you don't have to find it. But if your calendar is light, you do not sit and wait. You work the list, you set your own calls, and you get the deal on the books. We are hiring someone hungry: someone who sees a lead and lets nothing get in the way of closing it and collecting the cash.
 You own the deal end to end: outreach and call-setting when needed, discovery, audit review, proposal, objection handling, close, and cash collection. Deals are monthly retainers in the $3,000–$7,000/month range, sold to e-commerce owners and operators.
 Who you'll be selling to: e-commerce entrepreneurs whose businesses range from a couple million a year to a couple million a month. You need to be able to hold a sales conversation with them as a peer — without pedestalizing them.
 YOUR NUMBER
 Cash collected is the #1 KPI. Not calls booked, not proposals sent, not pipeline created — cash collected. Close rate, average deal size, speed to close, and pipeline hygiene all support that one number.
 WHAT YOU'LL DO
 • Run the full cycle on inbound and referred demand — first call to signature to payment.
 • Set your own calls when the calendar has room. Follow up relentlessly on no-shows, stalls, and old leads.
 • Diagnose a prospect's e-commerce business live on the call and connect it to what we do.
 • Build and present proposals for monthly retainers, handle objections, and get signatures.
 • Own collection — a signed deal that doesn't pay is not a closed deal.
 • Keep the CRM clean and current: every deal, every next step, every dollar.
 • Work with the delivery team so what you sell is what gets delivered.
 WHO THIS IS NOT FOR
 • You only work leads that are already on your calendar.
 • You need a manager to tell you what to do each morning.
 • You cut corners on admin — CRM notes, Slack updates, end-of-day reports.
 • Your experience is one-call, one-time-payment consumer sales with no retainer track record.
 • You avoid the money conversation.
 OUTCOMES & KPIS
 Steady state, after ramp:
 • $30,000+ in new MRR cash collected per month, minimum.
 • 6–8 closed retainers per month, at a $4,000–$5,000/month average deal size.
 • 100% of signed deals paid — a signed deal that doesn't pay is not a closed deal.
 • 25%+ live call close rate (calls held to signed).
 • Speed to close: first call to signature within 14 days on qualified deals.
 • Average deal size held at or above $4,000/month.
 • Supported by 4–5 qualified calls a day, 5 days a week (about 100 held calls a month), with enough open calendar space to absorb full inbound demand and self-set calls when the calendar is light.
 TIME & LOCATION
 • Full time, 30–40 hours a week, with freedom to build your own schedule — as long as there's enough open calendar space to hold 4–5 calls a day.
 • Available on Slack during core US business hours daily.
 WHAT YOU NEED
 This is a senior, high-trust seat, and we are being deliberately selective.
 • A track record closing recurring retainers in the $3,000–$7,000/month range (or higher), with numbers you can show: average deal size, close rate, cash collected.
 • Full sales cycle experience — you have set your own meetings, not just taken handed-off calls.
 • E-commerce experience is mandatory. You understand the numbers behind an e-commerce business, including CAC, LTV and funnel optimization.
 • Hands-on familiarity with at least one of: Amazon Ads, Facebook/Meta Ads, or Google Ads. You don't have to run campaigns, but you must hold a credible performance conversation.
 • B2B agency sales experience.
 • Based in the US, Canada, or UK, working US business hours.
 • A self-starter. That includes proactively studying — advertising, e-commerce, and B2B sales, daily.
 • Detailed and punctual. Our system is operations heavy: a clean and updated CRM, Slack, end-of-day reports, and the rest of the process are non-negotiable.
 • Comfortable being measured in public: cash collected, close rate, and pipeline hygiene are all visible.
 WHAT MAKES YOU STAND OUT
 • You've sold for an Amazon, Meta, Google, or TikTok performance agency.
 • You can read an ad account or P&L and speak to it live on a call.
 • You've carried a quota where the deal was a monthly commitment, not a one-time payment.
 • You've built pipelines from a cold list when inbound went quiet — and it worked.
 • You're coachable on our process and still bring your own frame to a call.
 COMPENSATION & BENEFITS
 • $145,000–$180,000 OTE.
 • 100% remote — work from anywhere in the US, Canada or UK.
 • Professional development and direct mentorship from leadership.
 • Join an 80+ person agency ranked Inc. 5000 #170, managing $24M+ in Amazon ad spend.
 * $5k draw for 60 days and full commission
